It has been speculated that the observed reductions in anabolism during times of low food availability may represent a conservation-oriented mechanism to spare ATP from unnecessary use given the energy-demanding nature of muscle protein synthesis (133). Importantly, insufficient energy intake results in an increased use of protein for fuel, regardless of protein consumption (127). That said, it is clearly possible to build muscle while losing body fat (i.e., in an energy deficit) as reported in the literature (23, 80); the extent of hypertrophy, however, will be less than that achieved in a caloric surplus.
